title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — corruption plus double reatus is unexampled as ‘sin’
pass_a_gloss: If you say the pre-law world-sin packs corruption together with reatus, which reatus? The one that follows corruption (sin pours guilt from itself), or the alleged antecedent reatus that makes corruption a penalty rather than sin? The latter cannot be shut out—so you get corruption flanked by two guilts, prior and following: a way of taking ‘sin’ no example proves.
pass_b_english: But if you say that the sin which was in the world until the law embraces corruption together with guilt, I will ask which guilt you mean: that which follows corruption (for sin, when it is, pours guilt from itself), or that which is said to precede corruption, and in respect of which corruption is not sin but the penalty of sin?

That latter certainly cannot be excluded: corruption will therefore be understood as attended with a double guilt, one antecedent, the other subsequent—a way of taking sin which can be proved by no example.
source_text: Quod si dicas, peccatum quod usque ad legem in mundo fuit, una cum reatu corruptionem complecti, quem intelligas reatum quaeram: illumne qui sequitur corruptionem (peccatum enim, cum sit, reatum a se fundit), an vero illum qui corruptionem antecedere dicitur, & cuius respectu corruptio non est peccatum, sed poena peccati? Ille certe excludi non potest: intelligetur igitur corruptio duplici stipata reatu, altero antecedente, altero subsequente, quomodo peccatum recipi aliquando, nullo exemplo probari potest.
